videos.script: Lesson twelve met three vector databases. This lesson meets three more tools, and they are less alike than their names suggest. {{three}} FAISS is a library. It holds vectors in memory and finds the nearest ones, and that is all it does. {{faiss}} It knows none of your ids, none of your metadata and none of your text. You will see what it hands back, and what you have to keep beside it. {{positions}} FAISS also names its indexes with short strings: Flat, HNSW, IVF, PQ. You will build four of them over twenty thousand vectors and compare their size and their recall. {{factory}} LanceDB is a database without a server. It keeps a table in columnar files on disk, and every write makes a new version you can go back to. {{lance}} Qdrant is usually a server. Its Python client also has a local mode that runs inside your program. That is what runs here, and you will find where it differs from the real thing. {{qdrant}} The lesson ends with the choice under all of this. An index inside your process, or a database at the other end of a network. {{choice}}
